request.gloss: submit a candidate's application

steps.note: The vacancy and what the school is looking for.
Accounts set the salary budget at the same time the vacancy is posted — the amount, or the range, the school is prepared to pay (BR-2). It is not posted without one (E1).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Where step 2 fails the vacancy exists in Draft and is not posted, and the budget is set again rather than the vacancy created twice.
plan.atomicity: Not atomic across the two steps. Step 1 creates the vacancy and step 2 sets its budget; it reaches the website only when both are done (BR-1, BR-2, E1). Posting it is public — candidates will apply against it, and every application is answered.

operations.purpose: Set the salary budget for the role and post the vacancy.

parameters.name: vacancy_id
parameters.notes: The vacancy created in step 1.

parameters.name: amount_or_range
parameters.notes: The amount, or the range, the school is prepared to pay (BR-2). Set by Accounts — a figure a planner produced is what the school will offer somebody.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The budget, and the vacancy posted.

fields.description: Posted. It is on the school website where candidates can find it (BR-1).

errors.meaning: The vacancy was posted with no salary budget.
errors.note: Accounts set it at the same time the vacancy is posted (BR-2).

planningRules.rule: Never draft the requirements. They go on the school's website and candidates apply against them (BR-1), and text a planner wrote is the school advertising terms nobody agreed.
Never supply the salary budget. It is what the school is prepared to pay somebody (BR-2), and the agreed salary is later recorded against it.
Never post without the budget. E1 is BR-2 working — a vacancy live with no figure behind it invites applications the school may not be able to meet.
Say plainly that posting is public. Candidates will apply against it, every application is answered, and none can be deleted while the vacancy is open (BR-9, BR-13).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Withdrawing the vacancy with a reason before it closes (A5). Applications already received stay on the record.

Report the candidates still without an outcome. They applied and are waiting, and a withdrawn vacancy does not answer them — each is owed a written explanation to the email on their form (BR-9, BR-11).

Never reject the candidates as part of the withdrawal. Each rejection carries its own written explanation (BR-9, E7), and one reason covering a field of applicants is not an explanation to any of them.
Never delete the applications. An application is never deleted while the vacancy is open (BR-13).

reversal.statement: A withdrawal is not undone. A post to be filled after all is advertised afresh, which is deliberate — the old candidates were told it was withdrawn.

A candidate is left with no outcome.
errors.note: The vacancy cannot be closed and the candidate has simply been forgotten (BR-9).

planningRules.rule: Never choose the candidate. The School Admin selects on what they saw at interview (BR-8), and a selection a planner made from marks has appointed somebody to a job.
Never compose the rejection explanations. Each is sent to that candidate as the school's account of why they did not get the job (BR-9, BR-11).
Report the candidates still without an outcome. The vacancy cannot be closed while any remains, and one forgotten is somebody who never hears back (BR-9, E8).
Never approve in the same plan. The recommender is never the approver (BR-8, E9), and the Principal sets the joining date on approval (BR-10).
Say plainly that nobody has been told. Candidates are notified when the outcome is approved (BR-11), and a selected candidate told early may resign a post on a decision nobody made.

reversal.statement: A recommendation is not withdrawn. The Principal returns it with a reason (A3), and where the selected candidate declines an alternative is recommended afresh (A4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An approval with no joining date, and an approval by the recommender, are both refused.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the approval, the joining date and the messages to every candidate together or not at all (BR-11). This is the moment the school tells people whether they have a job. The appointment does not create a staff record — that happens when the person actually joins (BR-12, UC-12-01 BR-1).

operations.name: vacancy.outcome.return

operations.purpose: Return the recommended outcome with the reason.

parameters.name: vacancy_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No vacancy matches within the actor's scope.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the vacancies with their role, closing date and status.

parameters.notes: The vacancy, resolved from its role and closing date.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Why the recommendation is not accepted. The School Admin recommends again from it.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Interviewing again. It sits with the School Admin.

fields.name: candidates_notified
fields.description: Zero. Nobody is told until an outcome is approved (BR-11).

errors.meaning: A recommendation was returned with no reason.
The vacancy is not awaiting approval.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. The School Admin recommends again from it, and a reason a planner wrote sends them back through a field of candidates on a guess.
Never notify any candidate of a return. They are told only when an outcome is approved (BR-11), and a rejected candidate told twice — once wrongly — cannot be untold.
Never name the alternative candidate. Recommending is the School Admin's act (BR-8), and a returned recommendation with a name attached is the approver making the selection.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A return is not withdrawn. The School Admin recommends again, with outcomes for every candidate, and it comes back for approval.
